Subject: Initial: TIA acceptance & procurement checklist questions

Hi David,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and legal at Acme are lining up the paperwork for the pilot. Before we start the signature path, a few practical questions we need answered to confirm the TIA (technical information assessment) side:

- Can you confirm whether the TIA evidence pack you provide includes a per-subprocessor inbound/outbound dataflow map (we need this for our dataflow annex)?
- For UK-bound data, do you rely on SCCs + UK Addendum or do you propose a UK IDTA signing route? Which artifacts do you typically supply for a UK Addendum proof (e.g., UK addendum execution example, subprocessors list with regions, KMS attestation)?
- Our procurement team will want a checklist we can attach to the PO that maps acceptance criteria to evidence (encryption at-rest/transit, HSM/KMS, logging retention, audit trail sample). Do you have a two-page acceptance checklist we can use?

We are targeting a Nov 8 start for the pilot if we can close signatures and evidence by Nov 4.

Appreciate a short reply and any sample artifacts.

Thanks,
Procurement (on behalf of Acme Health)

--
Acme Health Procurement Team

Hi —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then I’ll attach what we have.

- TIA evidence pack: yes, we provide a per-subprocessor dataflow map (CSV + visual) as part of the evidence pack.
- UK routing: we support both SCCs + UK Addendum and UK IDTA depending on customer preference. For pilots we often ship SCCs with our standard UK Addendum package; when customers require IDTA we coordinate execution via the same DocuSign flow and provide the additional attestation artifacts.
- Acceptance checklist: we have a concise procurement acceptance checklist — I’ll attach a version tailored for Acme that maps acceptance criteria to specific artifacts and locations in the evidence pack.

I’m attaching our current subprocessors export (redwood_subprocessors_2027Q3.csv) and a compact TIA evidence index (tia-evidence-pack-2027-10.pdf). Marissa is looped for privacy/contract artifacts and can confirm the UK Addendum examples.

Two quick clarifying Qs for you:
1) Do you need a redlined DPA or a fully executed DPA template in advance of the pilot? (some procurement teams want a redline before PO)
2) Does Acme require HSM-backed keys (customer-managed) for the pilot or is Redwood-managed KMS acceptable with contractual key control language?

I’ll also pull in Kimberly from legal for any execution exceptions.

Best,
David

Hi Lisa —

Quick note from privacy/contract side:
- We can provide a redline of our standard DPA within 48 business hours of receiving Acme’s preferred edits. Typical turnaround from our side after receiving a redline is 2–3 business days for initial review; final execution timing depends on signature queue.
- UK Addendum: attached to this thread is an example execution packet we provide customers (includes the addendum text, a sample execution page, and a checklist of supporting artifacts). For evidence we will supply: subprocessor list with region flags, KMS/HSM attestation (if applicable), logging/audit snapshot (sample), and the per-subprocessor dataflow CSV.
- HSM/KMS: we will accept contractual language for key separation; customer-managed HSM is an available escalation path but requires a separate onboarding window (typically 3–4 weeks). For a pilot, Redwood-managed KMS + contractual controls is the predictable path.

I’m attaching the tailored acceptance checklist (mutual-action-plan-acme-redwood.docx) — it maps the acceptance criteria you listed to specific files in the evidence pack and the DocuSign artifacts.

If Acme can sign off on the checklist and the PO by Nov 4, we can meet the Nov 8 pilot start with a limited data subset (non-production).

Regards,
Marissa

I’ll keep our legal response tight to the commercial items:
- Please send your redline (tracked edits) against our standard DPA to legal@redwood.com and we’ll prioritize. Aim for a single PDF with comments in the margin; anything larger than 10 substantive changes may require a short legal sync.

Hi Lisa / team —

A couple of technical clarifications to make the acceptance checklist operationally actionable:

1) Residency / routing: For the pilot we will pin model routing to EU-hosted pools (Frankfurt region) and provide a routing assertion document that lists the regional pools and fallback behavior. If a failover to our shared hosted tier occurs, the fallback is to a compatible EU model variant in a different zone — we will document SLOs and notify you in the mutual-action-plan.

2) KMS: Redwood-managed KMS is backed by a regional HSM cluster. We can provide a KMS attestation that includes key rotation cadence, access control lists, and dual-operator change controls. If Acme requests customer-managed keys, we will run a brief onboarding checklist (network reachability, grant of minimal IAM roles) and schedule a key handover — this path will add ~3 weeks.

3) Evidence handoff: the tia-evidence-pack-2027-10.pdf is the index. We will put the full evidence bundle in a restricted Drive folder and share a time-limited link. Any additional sample logs will be delivered as a blind-sampled CSV (redacted PII) per your request.

Action items we need from Acme to hit Nov 8:
- Signed PO referencing the mutual-action-plan doc by EOD Nov 4 (procurement)
- DPA redline submitted to legal@redwood.com by Nov 3 (legal)
- Confirmation whether you require customer-managed keys (yes/no) by Nov 3 (security/infra)

Once those items are in, we’ll create the DocuSign envelope with the UK Addendum and route for signature.

Thanks,
Jonas
